question: Which of the following statements regarding 'Navroz' (Nowruz) is **correct**?

options.text: It is a lunar-based festival celebrated exclusively by the Buddhist community in the Himalayan belt.
It is the Persian New Year celebrated on the Spring Equinox, introduced in India by Ghiyasuddin Balban.
It is a monsoon festival commemorating the victory of Good over Evil in the Mughal courts.
It marks the start of the harvest season in Southern India and is dedicated to the Sun God.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is the Persian New Year celebrated on the Spring Equinox, introduced in India by Ghiyasuddin Balban.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Navroz (Nowruz)** is the **Persian New Year**, celebrated on the **Spring Equinox**, which typically falls on **March 21** every year.
 
• It originated in ancient Persia and has its roots in **Zoroastrianism**, making it an important cultural and religious festival for Zoroastrians and Parsis.
 
• Navroz was introduced in India during the **Delhi Sultanate** by **Ghiyasuddin Balban** in the 13th century, who brought Persian traditions to Indian culture.
 
• The festival signifies the **renewal of nature**, the beginning of spring, and is celebrated with rituals, feasting, and cultural activities.
 
• Navroz is recognized as an **Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** by UNESCO and is celebrated in many countries, including India, Iran, Afghanistan, and parts of Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Characteristics of Navroz:**

 
 
• Navroz is a festival of **harmony, renewal, and gratitude**, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness.
 
• Preparations include **spring cleaning** of homes, buying new clothes, and decorating with flowers and rangoli.
 
• Families prepare a traditional table setting called **Haft-Seen**, which includes seven symbolic items starting with the Persian letter "S".
 
• Special dishes like **Sabzi Polo (herbed rice)** and sweets are prepared and shared with family and friends.
 
 
 
• **Other Observations:**
 
 
• It is a public holiday in countries like **Iran**, **Afghanistan**, and **Tajikistan**.
 
• In India, Navroz is primarily celebrated by the **Parsi community**, who follow Zoroastrian traditions.
 
• The festival also marks the start of the **new financial year** in some regions.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** Navroz is not a **lunar-based festival** nor exclusively celebrated by Buddhists. It is solar-based and linked to the Spring Equinox. (Incorrect)
 
• **Option 3:** Navroz is not a monsoon festival or associated with the Mughal courts. (Incorrect)
 
• **Option 4:** It does not mark the start of the harvest season in Southern India nor is it dedicated to the Sun God. (Incorrect)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO Recognition:** Navroz was inscribed in the **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in 2009.
 
• **Global Celebration:** The festival is celebrated in various forms across countries such as **Iran**, **India**, **Pakistan**, and **Central Asia**.
 
• **Zoroastrian Significance:** Navroz is deeply linked to **Zoroastrianism**, symbolizing the renewal of life and the triumph of good over evil.
 
• **Parsi Observances in India:** In India, Parsis offer prayers at fire temples and participate in community feasts.

• The **Delhi Sultanate** was divided into five dynasties: **the Slave Dynasty, the Khalji Dynasty, the Tughlaq Dynasty, the Sayyid Dynasty, and the Lodi Dynasty.**

question: Regarding the 'Subsidiary Alliance' system introduced by Lord Wellesley (1798–1805), which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: The ruler was free to employ any European (French, Portuguese, etc.) as long as they were not in active conflict with the British.
If the ruler failed to make payments for the maintenance of the British force, a portion of his territory was ceded as a penalty.
The British promised not to interfere in the internal administrative affairs of the allied state.
The Indian ruler was required to disband his own military and maintain a permanent British contingent within his territory.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The ruler was free to employ any European (French, Portuguese, etc.) as long as they were not in active conflict with the British.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Subsidiary Alliance** system was introduced by **Lord Wellesley** during his tenure as the Governor-General of India (1798–1805). It aimed to establish British dominance over Indian princely states.
 
• Under this system, the **Indian rulers were prohibited from employing any European in their service** other than the British. This clause was designed to prevent French and other European influences in India. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• If the ruler failed to make payments for the maintenance of the British forces stationed in their territory, they had to **cede a portion of their territory** as a penalty. *This statement is correct.*
 
• The British promised not to interfere in the internal administrative affairs of the allied state; however, this promise was often violated in practice. *This statement is correct.*
 
• The Indian ruler was required to **disband their own military** and maintain a permanent British military contingent within their territory. This ensured the dependency of the Indian ruler on the British. *This statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of the Subsidiary Alliance System:**

 
 
• The Indian rulers who accepted the alliance had to station a **British Resident** in their court. This gave the British significant control over the state's policies.
 
• The Indian states had to pay a subsidy for the maintenance of British troops stationed in their territory.
 
• The Indian rulers were essentially reduced to being **vassals** of the British, losing their sovereignty in external and defense matters.
 
 
 
• **States that Accepted the Alliance:**
 
 
• Major Indian states such as Hyderabad (1798), Mysore (1799), Awadh (1801), and the Marathas (1802) were compelled to accept the Subsidiary Alliance.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for the System:**
 
 
• To expand British political influence in India without engaging in direct annexation.
 
• To weaken potential rivals like the French and prevent Indian states from forming alliances with foreign powers.
 
 
 
• **Consequences of the Subsidiary Alliance:**
 
 
• The system led to the **gradual erosion of Indian princely states' power** and autonomy.
 
• It facilitated British control over a vast majority of India and laid the foundation for the establishment of direct British rule.
 
• Indian rulers became dependent on the British, leading to widespread discontent and resentment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lord Wellesley's Policy:** The Subsidiary Alliance was part of Lord Wellesley's broader policy of expansion and consolidation of British power in India.
 
• **Military Strategy:** The British used the stationed troops to suppress internal revolts and external threats in the allied states, ensuring their dominance.
 
• **Long-term Impact:** The system played a crucial role in the eventual establishment of the British Empire in India and the decline of regional powers.
 
• **Comparison with Doctrine of Lapse:** While the Subsidiary Alliance reduced the autonomy of princely states, the Doctrine of Lapse (introduced by Lord Dalhousie) directly annexed states without a male heir.

``

question: In which of the following years did Mahatma Gandhi led the Satyagraha and hunger strike for the first time in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1918**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi led the first Satyagraha and hunger strike in India in 1918.
 
• This event is known as the Ahmedabad mill workers.
 
• The Satyagraha was aimed at addressing the grievances of farmers who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions.
 
• Gandhi's leadership in this non-violent protest marked the beginning of his prominent role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The success of the Ahmedabad mill workers established the effectiveness of non-violent resistance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Champaran Satyagraha:**

 
 
• This was Gandhi's first active involvement in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was a major success and demonstrated the power of non-violent resistance (Satyagraha).
 
• Gandhi arrived in Champaran in 1917 and led the movement in 1918.
 
• It resulted in the abolition of the oppressive tinkathia system where farmers were forced to grow indigo on a portion of their land.
 
 
 
• **Satyagraha:**
 
 
• A form of non-violent resistance or civil resistance.
 
• The term was coined and developed by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It played a significant role in the Indian independence movement and influenced numerous other freedom and civil rights movements globally.
 
 
 
• **Indigo Cultivation:**
 
 
• Indigo was a cash crop grown in India during British rule.
 
• Farmers were often forced to grow indigo by British planters under oppressive conditions.
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha specifically addressed the exploitation and hardships faced by indigo farmers.
 
 
 
• **Non-violent Resistance:**
 
 
• A method of protest that seeks to achieve goals through symbolic protests, civil disobedience, and other non-violent means.
 
• Gandhi's philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) was central to his approach to resistance.
 
• Non-violent resistance has been adopted by various movements around the world, including the Civil Rights Movement in the United States.

• India conducted its first nuclear test, codenamed "Smiling Buddha," on **18 May 1974**, in Pokhran, Rajasthan.

• **Smiling Buddha**

• **Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Waterspouts are rotating columns of air and mist that form over a water body, commonly observed in tropical and subtropical regions.
 
• They are typically less intense and smaller in scale compared to tornadoes that form over land.
 
• Waterspouts are classified into two types: fair-weather waterspouts and tornadic waterspouts.
 
• Fair-weather waterspouts develop in relatively calm conditions, while tornadic waterspouts are associated with severe thunderstorms.
 
• Despite being less destructive, waterspouts can pose significant threats to small boats, swimmers, and coastal areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hurricanes**

 
 
• Hurricanes are large, powerful tropical cyclones that form over warm ocean waters, primarily in the Atlantic and Northeast Pacific.
 
• They are characterized by strong winds, heavy rains, and can cause significant damage to coastal and inland areas.
 
• Hurricanes are categorized on the Saffir-Simpson scale, ranging from Category 1 (least severe) to Category 5 (most severe).
 
 
 
• **Squalls**
 
 
• Squalls are sudden, sharp increases in wind speed, often accompanied by heavy rain, thunderstorms, or snow.
 
• They can occur in various weather systems, including cold fronts and tropical storms.
 
• Squalls can lead to hazardous conditions for marine and aviation activities.
 
 
 
• **Typhoons**
 
 
• Typhoons are the equivalent of hurricanes in the Northwest Pacific Ocean.
 
• They exhibit similar characteristics, including strong winds, heavy rainfall, and potential for widespread destruction.
 
• Typhoons are monitored and classified by the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and other regional meteorological organizations.

question: In 1962, who published 'The History of Ocean Basins', which outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, later called 'sea floor spreading'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harry Hammond Hess**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 1962, Harry Hammond Hess, **a geologist and Navy officer, published **'The History of Ocean Basins',** which **outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move**, later called **'sea floor spreading'.**
 
• **Hess **proposed that new ocean crust was** being continuously formed at mid-ocean ridges, where magma rises from the mantle and solidifies**, pushing older crust away from the ridge and eventually** causing it to subduct or be destroyed at deep-sea trenches.**
 
• This theory, which became known as** plate tectonics**, revolutionized the **field of geology and helped explain a wide range of geological phenomena**, **from the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes to the formation of mountains and the evolution of life on Earth.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plate Tectonic Theory:**

 
 
• Plate tectonic theory describes the movement of the **Earth's lithosphere, which is composed of several large and many smaller plates, driven by the convective motion of the mantle.**
 
• These plates move relative to one another, resulting in the formation of **new crust at mid-ocean ridges and the destruction of old crust at subduction zones.**
 
• This movement is responsible for a wide range of **geological phenomena, including the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes, the formation of mountain ranges, and the evolution of continents.**
 
• For example, the collision of the Indian and **Eurasian plates formed the Himalayas, and the separation of the African and South American plates created the Atlantic Ocean.**
 
• The theory also **explains the distribution of fossils, as species separated by the movement of plates evolved differently.**

question: Which letter code indicates mid-latitude desert climate in Köppen climate classification?
solution:
The correct answer is __**BWk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Köppen climate classification, **BWk** represents the mid-latitude desert climate.
 
• This climate type is characterized by **low annual precipitation**, typically less than 250 mm (10 inches).
 
• BWk climates usually have **hot summers and cold winters**, distinguishing them from the hot desert climates (BWh).
 
• Examples of regions with BWk climate include parts of the **Gobi Desert** in Mongolia and China.
 
• This classification helps in understanding the geographical distribution of arid and semi-arid regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Köppen Climate Classification**

 
 
• Developed by Vladimir Köppen, this classification system categorizes the world's climates based on temperature and precipitation.
 
• The main categories are Tropical (A), Dry (B), Temperate (C), Continental (D), and Polar (E).
 
• It is widely used in climatology, geography, and environmental science to study climate patterns.
 
 
 
• **Desert Climate (BWh)**
 
 
• Hot desert climates (BWh) have extremely high temperatures during the day and cool temperatures at night.
 
• These regions receive very little rainfall, often less than 250 mm annually.
 
• Examples include the Sahara Desert in Africa and the Arabian Desert in the Middle East.
 
 
 
• **Steppe Climate (BSk)**
 
 
• Steppe climates (BSk) are semi-arid regions that receive slightly more precipitation than deserts.
 
• These areas have hot summers and cool to cold winters.
 
• Examples include the Great Plains in the United States and the Eurasian Steppe.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change Impact**
 
 
• Climate change is altering precipitation patterns, potentially expanding desert and semi-arid areas.
 
• Understanding climate classifications helps in predicting and mitigating the impacts of climate change.
